question.:question/problem: What is the amplitude of the function $f(x)=2\left(\frac{5+8\cos(3x-1)}{9}\right)+1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)&=2\left(\frac{5+8\cos(3x-1)}{9}\right)+1\\&=\frac{2\cdot (8)}{9}\cdot \cos(3x-1)+\frac{2\cdot 5}{9}+1\\&=\frac{16}{9}\cdot \cos(3x-1)+\frac{19}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, given a function in the form $f(x)=A\cos(Bx+C)+D,$ the amplitude is $|A|.$

In our case, we have that $A=\frac{16}{9}.$ Therefore, the amplitude is $|A|=|\frac{16}{9}|=\frac{16}{9}.$

question.:question/problem: What is the amplitude of the function $f(x)=-3\left(\frac{8-10\sin(4x+1)}{7}\right)+3?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)&=-3\left(\frac{8-10\sin(4x+1)}{7}\right)+3\\&=\frac{-3\cdot (-10)}{7}\cdot \sin(4x+1)+\frac{-3\cdot 8}{7}+3\\&=\frac{30}{7}\cdot \sin(4x+1)-\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, given a function in the form $f(x)=A\sin(Bx+C)+D,$ the amplitude is $|A|.$

In our case, we have that $A=\frac{30}{7}.$ Therefore, the amplitude is $|A|=|\frac{30}{7}|=\frac{30}{7}.$
